# QS-CFW-5798-88 — Quality specification - crankshaft blank CFW-5798-88 (4340)
Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P2  
Parts: CFW-5798-88  
This revision supersedes Rev D.

Scope
- This quality specification applies to crankshaft blank CFW-5798-88 (4340) manufactured at Plant P2 and intended for subsequent machining and heat treatment operations at external or internal facilities. It defines the acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for receiving, in-process, and final inspection of the forged blank prior to release for downstream processing.

Background and rationale
- The material and geometry of CFW-5798-88 require control of core hardness, bore tolerance, and blank mass to ensure compatibility with downstream machining centers and final part requirements. The specified hardness range balances machinability and microstructural condition for successful heat treatment and finish grinding. The specified bore diameter tolerance ensures fitment to fixture bores used in machining operations without additional rework. The maximum forging weight is controlled to prevent overloading of handling equipment and to maintain consistency in forming parameters that affect internal soundness.

Requirements table

| Characteristic | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---:|---|
| Material designation | 4340 | Conforming mill certificate required |
| Hardness (as-forged core) | 25-29 HRC | Accept if within range; reject if outside range |
| Bore diameter tolerance | ±0.04 mm | Accept if measured within tolerance relative to drawing datum |
| Maximum forging weight | 119.4 kg | Do not accept blanks exceeding this mass |
| Surface condition | No visible laps, folds, or unbonded surface; light forging scale acceptable | Reject if surface discontinuities compromise geometry or machining allowance |
| Internal soundness | No indication of internal voids by method specified below | Reject if evidence of internal discontinuity is detected |

Inspection method
- Receiving inspection: Verify material certificate matches 4340 and traceability to heat lot. Physically verify identification marking against part serial. Measure mass using calibrated scales; record mass and compare to maximum forging weight of 119.4 kg. For any blank with mass exceeding 119.4 kg, segregate and initiate nonconformance procedure.
- Hardness measurement: Perform hardness testing on the as-forged core using a calibrated hardness tester appropriate for HRC scale. Take a representative reading in the mid-section of the crankshaft blank avoiding fillet radii and surface-affected zones. Report the measured value and verify it falls within 25-29 HRC. If a reading is outside 25-29 HRC, perform two additional measurements on nominally equivalent locations and record all readings. If any reading remains outside 25-29 HRC, follow nonconformance handling.
- Bore diameter measurement: Measure the bore diameter at the specified inspection plane using a calibrated bore gauge or plug gage capable of resolving to the required tolerance. Verify the measured diameter is within ±0.04 mm of the nominal drawing dimension at the inspection plane. Record the measurement method, instrument identification, and operator initials. If measurement uncertainty is suspected, perform a repeat measurement with an alternate calibrated instrument and document both results.
- Internal soundness inspection: Inspect for internal discontinuities using the non-destructive method specified in the drawing package. Record the inspection technique used and the operator identification. Any indication consistent with internal voids or laps is cause for rejection; document findings and proceed with nonconformance handling.
- Sampling and frequency: Determine inspection frequency based on the lot size and risk assessment performed by quality engineering. Document the chosen sampling plan and the rationale. Maintain records of the sampling plan in the part inspection folder.
- Calibration and instrument control: Ensure all measurement equipment used for mass, hardness, and bore measurement is within valid calibration. Record calibration certificate reference numbers in the inspection records.

Nonconformance handling
- Identification and segregation: Any blank failing to meet the requirements listed in the requirements table must be immediately identified, tagged, and segregated from conforming material to prevent inadvertent use. Use a nonconformance tag referencing this document id.
- Disposition options: Possible dispositions include rework, return to vendor, conditional acceptance for non-critical use, or scrap. Determine disposition based on root cause analysis, potential impact to fit and function, and consultation with the responsible engineering authority. For mass nonconformances exceeding the maximum forging weight of 119.4 kg, consider tooling and process review before dispositioning similar future pieces.
- Root cause and corrective action: For any nonconformance, perform a documented root cause analysis and implement corrective actions to prevent recurrence. Record corrective action assignments, responsible parties, and verification activities in the nonconformance record.
- Examples:
  - Example A: If a blank measures 24 HRC on initial hardness reading, perform two additional hardness measurements in equivalent locations. If the additional readings remain below the acceptable range of 25-29 HRC, record the measurements and initiate nonconformance handling to determine cause and disposition.
  - Example B: If a bore measurement shows a deviation beyond ±0.04 mm at the inspection plane, confirm instrument calibration and repeat measurement. If confirmed, segregate and document as nonconforming; investigate press and die condition for potential tooling wear.
- Records to keep: Maintain the following records in the part inspection folder: material mill certificate, mass measurement record (including instrument id), hardness test records (including instrument id and all readings), bore measurement records (including instrument id and drawing datum reference), internal soundness inspection report, calibration certificates for instruments used, nonconformance records, root cause analysis, and final disposition documentation. All records must reference QS-CFW-5798-88 and the applicable lot or serial identifiers for traceability.
- Review and release: Quality engineering shall review all inspection records before release of the blank for downstream processing. Release is permitted only when all specified requirements are met or a documented approved deviation exists.

End of document.
